nodes.name: BFS and DFS on a graph
nodes.description: Visit every reachable vertex once using a visited array: BFS goes level by level with a queue, DFS goes deep with recursion or a stack.

facets.recognize: Chooses BFS for levels and distances, DFS for exploring paths and structure.
facets.explain: Explains why both are O(V + E).
facets.implement: Marks vertices when they are pushed (BFS) or entered (DFS).
facets.trace: Can show the queue or call stack on a small graph.

misconceptions.desc: Marked vertices visited when popped instead of when pushed, queueing them many times.
Kept no visited array, looping forever on cycles.
Cannot explain why BFS and DFS are O(V + E).

nodes.name: Counting connected components
nodes.description: Start a traversal from every unvisited vertex; each start is a new component.

facets.recognize: Maps provinces, islands and groups onto connected components.
facets.implement: Counts once per new start and handles adjacency-matrix input.

misconceptions.desc: Incremented the count inside the traversal instead of once per start.
Treated an adjacency matrix like an edge list, or mishandled the diagonal.

nodes.name: Grids as graphs
nodes.description: Each cell is a vertex with 4 (or 8) neighbours; direction arrays and a bounds check replace the adjacency list.

facets.recognize: Sees islands, regions and fills as graph traversal on cells.
facets.implement: Uses direction arrays and checks bounds before reading a cell.
facets.adapt: Handles 8 directions, regions connected to the border and shape signatures.

misconceptions.desc: Read a neighbour before checking it is inside the grid.
Got the direction arrays wrong (a direction missing, or diagonals where only 4 are allowed).
In flood fill, recursed forever when the new colour equals the old one.
Searched from every inner cell instead of starting from the border for boundary-connected regions.
Recorded absolute coordinates for island shapes instead of coordinates relative to the start cell.

nodes.name: Multi-source BFS
nodes.description: Push every source into the queue at time 0; one BFS then gives each cell its distance to the nearest source.

facets.recognize: Spots 'nearest of many sources' and 'spreads every minute' problems.
facets.explain: Explains why starting all sources together gives nearest distances.
facets.implement: Seeds the queue with all sources, counts time per level and detects unreachable cells.

misconceptions.desc: Ran a separate BFS from every source (O(k * n * m)).
Counted time per popped cell instead of per level, or was off by one at the end.
Did not detect cells that are never reached.

nodes.name: Cycle detection in an undirected graph
nodes.description: During BFS or DFS, reaching an already-visited vertex that is not the parent means a cycle.

facets.explain: Explains why the edge back to the parent does not count.
facets.implement: Tracks the parent and checks every component.

misconceptions.desc: Did not track the parent, so the edge back to it looked like a cycle.
Checked only the first component.

nodes.name: Cycle detection in a directed graph
nodes.description: DFS with an 'on the current path' mark: an edge to a vertex on the path is a cycle. Kahn's algorithm finds one when not every vertex is removed.

facets.explain: Explains why plain visited is not enough in a directed graph.
facets.implement: Sets and clears the path mark, or counts Kahn's removed vertices.
facets.adapt: Finds eventual safe states (vertices that cannot reach a cycle).

misconceptions.desc: Used only the visited array, reporting a cycle when two paths reach the same vertex.
Did not clear the path mark when DFS returned.
Applied the parent-check method meant for undirected graphs.

nodes.name: Bipartite check
nodes.description: Colour a vertex, give every neighbour the opposite colour; a neighbour with the same colour means the graph is not bipartite.

facets.explain: Explains that a graph is bipartite exactly when it has no odd cycle.
facets.implement: Colours with BFS or DFS from every uncoloured vertex.

misconceptions.desc: Coloured only from vertex 0, missing other components.
Cannot explain the link between bipartite graphs and odd cycles.

nodes.name: Topological sort
nodes.description: Order a DAG so every edge points forward: reverse DFS finish order, or Kahn's algorithm removing in-degree-0 vertices.

facets.recognize: Spots ordering with prerequisites (courses, build steps, alien alphabets).
facets.explain: Explains why it exists only for DAGs.
facets.implement: Builds edges in the right direction and checks every vertex was ordered.
facets.adapt: Builds the alien-dictionary graph from the first differing letters of adjacent words.

misconceptions.desc: Built prerequisite edges in the wrong direction.
Returned an order without checking that every vertex was included.
In alien dictionary, missed the invalid case where a word comes before its own prefix.
Used DFS order without reversing the finish order.
Applied topological sort to an undirected or cyclic graph.

nodes.name: Shortest paths with unit weights
nodes.description: In an unweighted graph BFS reaches each vertex first along a shortest path: dist[v] = dist[u] + 1.

facets.recognize: Uses BFS, not DFS, for fewest-steps questions.
facets.implement: Sets distances when vertices are pushed.
facets.adapt: Generates neighbours on the fly (word ladder, state spaces) and records all shortest paths.

misconceptions.desc: Used DFS to find a shortest path in an unweighted graph.
In word ladder, compared every pair of words (O(n² L)) instead of trying one-letter changes against a set.
In word ladder II, erased words when first seen instead of after the level, losing other shortest paths.

nodes.name: Shortest paths in a DAG
nodes.description: Relax edges in topological order; it works even with negative weights because there are no cycles.

facets.explain: Explains why topological order makes one relaxation pass enough.

misconceptions.desc: Relaxed edges out of vertices that were never reached (distance still infinity).
Relaxed in arbitrary order instead of topological order.

nodes.name: Dijkstra's algorithm
nodes.description: Repeatedly settle the closest unsettled vertex from a min-heap and relax its edges; weights must be non-negative.

facets.recognize: Uses Dijkstra for weighted shortest paths with non-negative weights.
facets.explain: Explains why the closest heap entry is final, and why that fails with negative weights.
facets.implement: Uses a min-heap of (distance, vertex), skips stale entries and stores distances in long long when needed.
facets.adapt: Adapts the cost (max edge on the path), counts shortest paths and adds state (stops) when required.

misconceptions.desc: Did not skip stale heap entries (d > dist[u]).
Used the default max-heap.
Applied Dijkstra to a graph with negative weights.
When counting shortest paths, reset or added the count at the wrong time (equal distance adds, shorter resets).
For cheapest flights within k stops, kept only the best distance, discarding cheaper-later paths with fewer stops.
Summed distances in int and overflowed.

nodes.name: Bellman-Ford
nodes.description: Relax every edge V - 1 times; if one more pass still improves a distance, there is a negative cycle.

facets.explain: Explains why V - 1 rounds suffice and what the extra round detects.
facets.implement: Relaxes only from reached vertices and runs the detection round.

misconceptions.desc: Ran fewer than V - 1 rounds.
Relaxed from unreached vertices (infinity + w).
Did not run the extra round to detect a negative cycle.

nodes.name: Floyd-Warshall
nodes.description: dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j]) with k as the outermost loop gives all-pairs distances in O(V³).

facets.explain: Explains why k must be the outermost loop.
facets.implement: Initializes the matrix, guards infinite sums and checks the diagonal for negative cycles.

misconceptions.desc: Put k in an inner loop.
Added two infinite distances and overflowed.
Did not set dist[i][i] = 0, or missed negative cycles shown by dist[i][i] < 0.

nodes.name: Minimum spanning tree
nodes.description: Prim grows one tree using a heap of crossing edges; Kruskal adds edges by increasing weight, skipping those that join already-connected vertices.

facets.explain: Explains why the cheapest crossing edge is always safe to add.
facets.implement: Writes Prim with a visited check on pop, or Kruskal with union-find.

misconceptions.desc: In Prim, marked vertices when pushed instead of popped, or added an edge to a vertex already in the tree.
In Kruskal, did not skip edges whose ends are already connected.
Confused a minimum spanning tree with a shortest-path tree.

nodes.name: Solving problems with union-find
nodes.description: Unite elements that belong together, then answer with the number or size of components; map cells or names to integer ids first.

facets.recognize: Uses union-find for connectivity that grows over time or groups defined by shared keys.
facets.implement: Maps items to ids consistently and counts components as unions succeed.
facets.adapt: Handles islands added one by one, merged accounts and flipping one cell to join islands.

misconceptions.desc: Mapped cells or names to ids inconsistently (cell id is row * cols + col).
For connecting a network, did not compare spare edges with components - 1.
In making a large island, added the same neighbouring component twice.
Re-ran a full traversal after every update instead of uniting incrementally.

nodes.name: Bridges and articulation points
nodes.description: DFS records each vertex's discovery time and the lowest time reachable from its subtree: (u, v) is a bridge if low[v] > tin[u]; u is an articulation point if low[v] >= tin[u] (the root needs two children).

facets.explain: Explains what low[v] means and why the two conditions differ.
facets.implement: Skips the parent edge and treats the DFS root specially.

misconceptions.desc: Used the edge back to the parent to update low.
Treated the DFS root like any other vertex for articulation points.
Used >= for bridges or > for articulation points.

nodes.name: Strongly connected components
nodes.description: DFS to get a finish order, reverse every edge, then DFS in decreasing finish order on the reversed graph; each DFS is one component.

facets.explain: Explains why reversing edges stops a DFS from leaking into other components.
facets.implement: Builds the reversed graph and runs the second pass in decreasing finish order.

misconceptions.desc: Ran the second pass on the original graph.
Ran the second pass in increasing instead of decreasing finish order.
